artboards.title: A — Premium SaaS (what is live now)

annotations.text:
FOUR DIRECTIONS FOR THE LANDING PAGE

Each one is clickable — try the control in it before you judge it.
A: the product tabs. B: the বাংলা / English switch. C: the filters.
D: the questions.

All four use real HelloStudents content: real batch names, real ৳ fees,
the real 85/15 split. Nothing here is invented about the product.

A — PREMIUM SAAS
The incumbent, tightened. Included so the others get judged against something, not against memory.

FOR: signals "serious software". Familiar to anyone who has seen Linear or Stripe.

AGAINST: it looks like every other SaaS site, and it says nothing about Bangladesh. Teachers are not SaaS buyers — a coaching-centre teacher has never seen a page like this and has no reason to trust it.

B — BENGALI-FIRST
বাংলা leads, English is the toggle. Warm paper instead of the indigo wash. Three plain steps instead of a feature grid.

FOR: it speaks to the person who actually signs up. The three-step block answers the real question — "what do I actually do?"

AGAINST: two languages of copy to write and maintain forever. And some tutors read English-language design as higher status; this may read as downmarket to them.

C — PROOF-FIRST
No hero at all. You land in the live batch list, and the filters work.

FOR: the product is the pitch. A visiting teacher sees peers charging ৳2,500 and keeping 85% — that is more persuasive than any headline.

AGAINST: with one published batch today this page looks abandoned. It only works once the marketplace is genuinely full, and it gives a cold visitor no story.

D — EDITORIAL TRUST
Aimed at the parent, not the student. Serif, quiet, one column. The four questions are the page.

FOR: education is a trust purchase, and a parent handing over ৳2,500 a month has exactly these four worries. Every answer is true of what you have built — approval, refunds, watermarking, 85/15.

AGAINST: quiet. No energy, nothing to screenshot, and it may read as old-fashioned to a 17-year-old picking their own batch.
